drug_class: Combination topical medication: Vitamin D3 analog plus corticosteroid
purpose: This medication is used to treat plaque psoriasis, which is a skin condition that causes thick, scaly, red patches on your skin. It helps reduce the redness, flaking, and itching that comes with psoriasis. It is applied directly to the affected areas on your skin or scalp.
how_it_works: This medicine has two active ingredients that work together as a team. The calcipotriene part is a form of Vitamin D that helps slow down the overactive skin cell growth that causes those thick, scaly plaques. The betamethasone part is a steroid that calms down the inflammation and reduces the redness, swelling, and itching in the affected area.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include skin irritation, itching, or burning where you apply the medication. Some people notice their skin becomes dry or develops a rash. You may also see some temporary skin lightening in the areas where you use it.
warnings: Do not use this medication on your face, underarms, or groin unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Avoid getting it in your eyes or mouth. Using too much or for too long can thin your skin or cause stretch marks. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages or wraps without asking your doctor. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medication.
typical_dosing: Adults typically apply this medication to the affected skin areas once daily. For the foam or topical suspension form, you usually apply it to the scalp or skin once a day for up to 4 to 8 weeks. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to use and for how long. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
